title: service-account-refresh-role-crossover-and-audit-tag-reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalation: a large enterprise reported two related failures during service account token refresh after a SAML group membership update. Symptoms: (1) users temporarily received expanded write privileges on a subset of projects (over-permission) for ~4-8 minutes after token refresh, and (2) audit logs for those actions omitted the SAML assertion metadata (idp_group, assertion_id), making post-incident forensics difficult. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a permanent fix that reconciles role assignment ordering with audit-tag propagation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has long-lived service account S that uses automatic token refresh linked to SAML assertion mapping
2) Admin updates SAML group->role mapping in IdP and triggers group sync
3) Service account undergoes refresh cycle while sync is mid-flight; server accepts new assertion A and applies role merge logic
4) Due to our concurrent role resolution, ephemeral higher-privilege bindings from assertion A are applied before the final deny-based mapping is reconciled

5) Audit pipeline deduplicates events and drops assertion context because assertion_id matched a recent stale entry, resulting in audit entries that show 'service_account: S performed X' with no idp metadata
root_cause: Two interacting bugs: (A) role-merge algorithm applies additive permissions from a freshly accepted SAML assertion before the later deny/overwrite step runs when membership sync completes; (B) the audit enrichment/dedup component suppresses assertion metadata for high-throughput refreshes by merging events on assertion_id without validating final resolution state. Together these produce transient over-grant windows with incomplete audit context.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed: serialized refresh handler so a given service account cannot have overlapping refresh applications on the role graph (decreases concurrency window)
Temporary policy: increase token TTL for affected orgs to reduce refresh frequency while long-term fix is being tested
Customer communication: notified affected customers, provided timestamped list of suspect operations, and offered support for audit reconstruction
fix_plan: 1) Change role resolution ordering to compute final intended bindings atomically before applying to the live permission cache
2) Update audit enrichment to attach the latest assertion_id and idp_group only after resolution completes; remove dedup merge on assertion_id when resolution state is uncertain
3) Add unit + integration tests simulating concurrent group sync + token refresh with assertions replayed to ensure no transient over-permit windows
4) Smoke run on staging with synthetic high-frequency refresh load for 24h, validate metrics: 'transient_overgrant_count'=0 and 'audit_enrichment_miss_rate'<0.1%
5) Roll out canary to 10% of orgs then full rollout, monitor audit gaps and permission-change metrics
regressions: None observed in staging. Hotfix introduced a 0.2% increase in refresh latency under peak which is within SLA; will monitor.
audit_log_gap_examples: 2025-02-07T14:24:33Z - project:beta - service_account:S - action:modify_route - assertion_id present but later audit shows truncated metadata
